questions.q: Why can accepting help be good for the giver?
a: Helping others lets them process their own problems
It creates a debt they can call in later
It makes them look generous to others
It teaches them skills they lack
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Anthony, who found helping Palmer helped him too.

questions.q: What separates an ask from begging?
a: An ask leaves the other person free to say no
An ask always includes a gift in return
An ask is made only to close friends
An ask is repeated until it succeeds
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a real ask is a two-way street with a viable no.

questions.q: What did Palmer learn from offering flowers to her audience?
a: A true gift must let the other person decline it
People value gifts more when they cost money
Audiences prefer gifts they can keep
Offering gifts creates loyal customers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says some people refused, which made the exchange a real ask.

questions.q: How did Palmer treat her email list?
a: Like pen pals she could share everything with
Like a sales funnel to convert into buyers
Like a private archive of fan data
Like a mailing list to sell to partners
questions.why: Lesson 3 says she was making friends, not collecting customers.

questions.q: Why did she refuse to hand her list to her managers?
a: She feared they would commercialize and spam it
She wanted to sell it to a higher bidder
She had promised it to her bandmates
She worried it was too small to matter
questions.why: Lesson 3 says she would not sell out her friends for efficiency.
